deep_dive_html:
The Perils of Unregulated CAM Pass-Throughs

For restaurant operators, the Common Area Maintenance (CAM) clause is often the most volatile component of a commercial lease. While tenants expect to pay their pro-rata share of shared expenses, landlords frequently exploit 'operating expense' definitions to shift the burden of long-term property value enhancement onto the tenant. This is often achieved by blurring the line between routine maintenance and capital improvements.

The primary trap lies in the inclusion of capital expenditures within the definition of recoverable expenses. A sophisticated landlord may attempt to pass through the cost of a new roof, parking lot repaving, or HVAC replacement—items that increase the landlord's equity—under the guise of 'maintenance.' Furthermore, many leases include 'management fees' or 'administrative charges' calculated as a percentage of gross rents, which can lead to a compounding spiral of costs that have nothing to do with the actual upkeep of the premises.

Implementing Market-Standard Protections

To protect your restaurant's bottom line, your lease must contain specific, enforceable limitations. An elite-level lease negotiation should focus on three critical pillars:

  • Expense Caps: Negotiate a 'cumulative cap' on the annual increase of controllable operating expenses. This prevents year-over-year spikes from destabilizing your cash flow.
  • Capital Expenditure Exclusions: Explicitly exclude any costs related to the replacement of structural elements or major systems. If a landlord must replace a roof, that should be amortized over its useful life and only charged to the tenant for the portion of the useful life occurring during the lease term.
  • Audit Rights and Verification: Ensure the lease grants you the right to audit the landlord's books and records. Without the right to verify the accuracy of CAM reconciliations, you are essentially signing a blank check.

Navigating these complexities requires more than just a cursory reading; it requires a forensic examination of the fine print. Do not let hidden costs erode your restaurant's profitability.
